claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase disordered solid solution after standard melting and solution heat treatment.
HfNbTaTiZr possesses intrinsic atomic-scale lattice distortions arising from its disordered structure.
Increasing temperature increases the amplitude of atomic vibrations in HfNbTaTiZr.
Increasing temperature increases the anharmonicity of the alloy's lattice vibrations or interatomic response.
Temperature-activated anharmonic vibrations partially relax the alloy's intrinsic lattice distortions.
The intrinsic lattice distortions obstruct dislocation motion at room temperature.
Relaxation of lattice distortions lowers barriers to dislocation motion.
Lower barriers to dislocation motion reduce the yield strength at elevated temperature.
Elevated temperature increases interatomic spacing in HfNbTaTiZr.
Anharmonic vibration-induced relaxation produces a higher apparent coefficient of thermal expansion.
Elevated-temperature HfNbTaTiZr will have lower yield strength than the room-temperature baseline.
Elevated-temperature HfNbTaTiZr will have a lower elastic modulus than the room-temperature baseline.
Elevated-temperature HfNbTaTiZr will show greater thermal expansion than the room-temperature baseline.
The predicted softening is expected to be especially evident above approximately 900°C.
The proposed response regime extends from room temperature to approximately 1200°C.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the alloy remains a single-phase disordered solid solution without phase transformation, significant oxidation, or phase separation.
The quantitative changes in yield strength, elastic modulus, and thermal-expansion coefficient depend on processing history and microstructural details.
